problem: If $sin⁡\theta =\frac{7}{8}$ and $\frac{\pi }{2}<\theta <\pi $ then what is the value of $sec⁡\theta ?$
worked_solution:
Let's sketch our angle $\theta $ in the coordinate plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932638/assets/5c98414bbe0e1e373864e9ec1d6b8667bb0032c8824f20bed1e6f9b9079c4d02.png)

We're given that $sin⁡\theta =\frac{7}{8}.$ We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{7}{8}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{7}{8})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{49}{64}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{15}{64}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{15}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is negative in the second quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =-\frac{\sqrt{15}}{8}.$

Finally, knowing that $sec⁡\theta =\frac{1}{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
sec⁡\theta =\frac{1}{(-\frac{\sqrt{15}}{8})}=-\frac{8}{\sqrt{15}}=-\frac{8\sqrt{15}}{15}.
$$
